File the plan with IHDA within 60 days; implementation report no later than four years after adoption/update; prior plans require progress summaries.

states.name: Utah
states.plan_mandate: Each municipality must prepare and adopt a comprehensive, long-range general plan under §10-20-401.
states.housing_duty: Specified municipalities must include a moderate-income housing element meeting §10-21-201. Other municipalities are encouraged to address moderate-income housing.
states.coverage: Cities of the first through fourth classes (population at least 10,000), plus fifth-class cities with population at least 5,000 in first-, second- or third-class counties (county population at least 40,000). A municipality newly qualifying as of January 1 must amend its plan by August 1 that year. Fixed-guideway public-transit stations trigger additional strategy requirements.
states.allocation_detail: The municipality analyzes how it will give a realistic opportunity to meet additional moderate-income housing needs during the next five years. The reviewed provisions prescribe strategy menus and implementation duties, not an externally allocated regional unit share.

contents.detail: Analyze the municipality's additional moderate-income housing needs for the next five years and realistic opportunities to meet them.
The element focuses on moderate-income housing, defined as affordable at 80% of county median gross household income, adjusted for household size.

Without a fixed-guideway station: select at least three listed strategies, or at least one of the special housing-zone/density-bonus strategies (X)–(CC). With a station: five including station-area planning and specified transit-density or parking reform, or the alternative three-strategy combination. Adopt a five-year implementation timeline with specific benchmarks.

Specified municipalities report implementation actions and barriers, ADUs, entitlements, building permits, occupancy and zoning information. The ordinary report is due August 1; 2026 has a statutory reporting pause and carryover compliance, with a separate July 1 occupancy-count requirement.
Strategies can address zoning, fees, parking, infrastructure and approvals; no single reform is universally required because municipalities choose among statutory alternatives.

states.enforcement: State review determines compliance and allows cure and appeal. Noncompliance can cause specified transportation-funding ineligibility and daily fees; the statute also authorizes injunctive enforcement. The 2026 reporting pause preserves qualifying 2025 compliance; normal implementation reporting resumes in 2027.
states.key_distinction: This is a mandatory planning-and-strategy system for a population-defined subset, not a California-style assigned unit obligation. The 2025 recodification and July 2026 amendments make older §10-9a citations and older strategy counts incomplete.

evidence.reasoning: General plans are universal, but §403 mandates the moderate-income element specifically for defined specified municipalities.
The definition's municipal and county classes translate to the precise thresholds stated; §403 supplies the newly qualifying deadline.
Section 201 requires local five-year needs analysis and chosen strategies; it does not assign cities a state or regional numerical need.
The effective July 2026 text contains the report pause and carryover rules, which qualify the ordinary annual reporting requirement.
Section202 provides compliance review, cure/appeal, funding consequences, fees and injunctive enforcement, with a 2026 reporting exception.
